name: Random Forest - Unemployment Prediction in Vienna Districts v1.0
description: Random Forest regression pipeline (StandardScaler + RandomForestRegressor) trained to predict the average annual number of unemployed persons (age 15-64) in Vienna districts using guest overnight stays and average population as predictors, with one-hot-encoded district codes as additional features. Hyperparameters selected by exhaustive grid search (36 combinations) on the validation set. Best-performing model of the experiment; serialized as model_random_forest_v1.0.pkl.
fair4ml:modelCategory: Supervised learning; Ensemble method; Random Forest Regression; scikit-learn Pipeline (StandardScaler + RandomForestRegressor)
description: Hyperparameters (selected by grid search on validation RMSE): n_estimators=200, max_depth=None (fully grown trees), min_samples_split=2, random_state=42, n_jobs=-1. Search space: n_estimators in [100,200,300], max_depth in [3,5,10,None], min_samples_split in [2,5,10] (36 combinations). Final model retrained on combined train+validation data (391 rows, 2002-2018) after selection.

fair4ml:trainedOn.name: TU Wien DBRepo - Unemployment and Tourism Experiment Database (train_split + validation_split, 2002-2018, 391 rows)
fair4ml:trainedOn.description: Combined DBRepo views 'train_split' (2002-2015, 322 rows) and 'validation_split' (2016-2018, 69 rows) used for final model fit after hyperparameter selection. Features: TOU_VALUE, POP_AVE, DISTRICT_CODE (one-hot encoded, 23 binary columns). Target: UEP_VALUE. COVID years 2020-2021 and district 90000 excluded.

fair4ml:validatedOn.name: TU Wien DBRepo - Unemployment and Tourism Experiment Database (validation_split view, 2016-2018, 69 rows)
fair4ml:validatedOn.description: Used for hyperparameter grid search selection (minimum validation RMSE criterion).

fair4ml:testedOn.name: TU Wien DBRepo - Unemployment and Tourism Experiment Database (test_split view, 2019/2022/2023, 69 rows)
fair4ml:testedOn.description: Held-out test set. Years 2019, 2022, 2023 across 23 Vienna districts.

fair4ml:hasEvaluation.name: Random Forest Test Set Evaluation

fair4ml:evaluationMetrics.name: RMSE
fair4ml:evaluationMetrics.measurementTechnique: Root Mean Squared Error (sqrt of sklearn.metrics.mean_squared_error)

fair4ml:hasEvaluation.fair4ml:evaluationResults: R²=0.9362, RMSE=~1189.99, MAE=~684.89 on test years 2019/2022/2023. The model predicts well for low-to-medium unemployment values but underestimates districts with UEP_VALUE above ~5,000, indicating that tourism and population alone are insufficient to explain high structural unemployment.

fair4ml:intendedUse: Prediction of district-level annual unemployment counts in Vienna. Intended for research and educational use. Can serve as a baseline for more complex socio-economic forecasting pipelines. Not intended for deployment in policy or administrative decision-making without further validation.
fair4ml:modelRisksBiasLimitations: Only two numeric predictors (tourism overnight stays and average population) are used; socio-economic factors such as industry composition, education levels, wage levels, or housing costs are excluded. COVID years 2020-2021 are excluded; the model has not been validated on pandemic-period data. High-unemployment districts (UEP_VALUE > ~5,000) are predicted with lower accuracy. No cross-validation was performed - a single chronological split is used. One-hot encoding of district codes makes the model non-transferable to new or renamed districts without retraining. serialized with scikit-learn 1.7.2; loading with a different version may produce unexpected behaviour.
fair4ml:legal: Training data sourced from Austrian Open Government Data under CC BY 4.0. Model artefact released under MIT License.
fair4ml:ethicalSocial: The model predicts unemployment, a sensitive socio-economic indicator. Predictions should not be used to label or rank districts in public-facing applications without appropriate contextualisation. The model captures correlation between tourism and unemployment and does not imply causation.
fair4ml:usageInstructions: Load the trained pipeline with joblib.load('outputs/models/model_random_forest_v1.0.pkl'). Prepare input features: TOU_VALUE (int), POP_AVE (int), DISTRICT_CODE one-hot encoded using the same OneHotEncoder fitted during training (23 binary columns). Call model.predict(X) to obtain UEP_VALUE predictions.
fair4ml:codeSampleSnippet:
import joblib
model = joblib.load('outputs/models/model_random_forest_v1.0.pkl')
y_pred = model.predict(X_test)  # X_test: [TOU_VALUE, POP_AVE, DISTRICT_90100, ..., DISTRICT_92300]
